entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. Home, Lucknow Counsel for Applicant :- Om Prakash Verma,Akash Dikshit

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. It is argued by the counsel for the applicant that the co-accused has been enlarged on bail.
It is further argued that in terms of the FIR, it was alleged that the marriage was solemnized around five years ago.

It is further argued that the applicant was serving at Punjab on the date of the incident and further more there are no allegation against the applicant of causing any mental or physical harassment to the deceased in relation to the demand of dowry soon before the death of the deceased.
In the post mortem report the cause of death is ante mortem hanging.

He further argues that the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 05.05.2023, as such, the applicant Raju vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. ... on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14036301/
1 may be enlarged on bail.

entities.text: Raju vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.

4. Considering the aforesaid facts coupled with the fact that the co-accused has been enlarged on bail, the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 05.05.2023 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant Raju be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.190 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Antu, District Pratapgarh, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 16.2.2024 Arun  Raju vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Deptt. ... on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14036301/
